title: Semantic exhaustion: extraction of meaning outrunning its replenishment
description: These claims hold that semantic exhaustion is underway: extraction of meaning exceeds replenishment across human, institutional and model substrates, and model collapse is the same crisis in another substrate. They set out measures such as the Semantic Debt Ratio, Exhaustion Proximity Index and Regeneration Capacity Assessment, and predict quality loss concentrated in high-Γ domains, platform capture of interpretive frameworks and burnout tracking semantic rent. The Anthropological Limit, the Pergamon Press theses, the Sorting Function and the commons-depletion thresholds supply historical theses on enclosure of the knowledge commons and on non-predatory mediation at scale.

## Measurement
### Semantic Debt Ratio (SDR)


SDR = E / R

Where:
E = Semantic extraction (value derived)
R = Semantic replenishment (value returned)

SDR >> 1 indicates exhaustion trajectory

### Exhaustion Proximity Index (EPI)


EPI = 1 - (Cₜ / C₀)

Where:
Cₜ = Current semantic capital
C₀ = Initial semantic capital

EPI approaching 1 = exhaustion imminent

### Regeneration Capacity Assessment (RCA)


RCA = Rₘₐₓ / E

Where:
Rₘₐₓ = Maximum sustainable replenishment rate
E = Current extraction rate

RCA < 1 = unsustainable (exhaustion inevitable without intervention)
RCA ≥ 1 = sustainable (regeneration can match extraction)
